**Indikator 1** is a quality indicator within the DANIBD (Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease) registry system, designed to measure and track the quality of patient investigations. However, its current implementation has drawn criticism from regional healthcare providers for failing to provide an accurate reflection of clinical investigation quality. According to regional feedback in the DANIBD 2024 annual report, the indicator's data capture is not yet fully optimized, which leads to skewed performance metrics and misrepresents hospital efforts.

To understand these discrepancies, [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] conducted an internal audit of patients who did not fulfill the criteria for Indikator 1 [^src1]. The audit revealed two primary reasons for the apparent shortfall in the data. First, a significant portion of these patients had already received sufficient investigation at other hospitals, meaning no further investigation was required or performed at Aarhus [^src1]. Second, in several other cases, patients explicitly declined to undergo a colonoscopy [^src1]. Because the inclusion of these specific patient groups skews the metrics, the hospital concluded that until data capture mechanisms are optimized, Indikator 1 does not provide a true or fair picture of the quality of investigations performed [^src1]. This critical evaluation highlights how the DANIBD database is actively used by hospitals and regions not just as a passive national registry, but as a dynamic management and audit tool for local quality improvement in IBD treatment.
